text:
sara_sales: Hey team — enterprise prospect (FinTech Co) asked for a CAIQ + a mapped shared-responsibility diagram for data flows. They want explicit ownership for KMS, logging/retention, backups, model artefacts, and outputs. Can SE/security help? cc @ali_se @mike_security

ali_se: On it. Do we have a canonical diagram? I can sketch a mapping to the CAIQ sections. Need to confirm if POC will be Hosted API, Dedicated, or Private — that changes KMS and network ownership.

jamie_csm: They're planning Hosted API with a Dedicated pool for the POC (2-week trial-ish). Regulator asks: no raw PII persisted and CMEK for keys where possible.

mike_security: Quick notes: for Hosted+Dedic we own runtime infra and model weights; customer owns inputs/prompts and customer-side IAM. KMS: CMEK supported for Dedicated and Private. Hosted default is provider-managed keys; BYOK for Hosted requires legal/OPS integration (we can offer via contract for enterprise). Logging: we can redact or disable full-text logs on request; audit trails still retained per retention policy. Backups: only infra/model snapshots by Redwood; customer data isn't mirrored unless they opt-in for ingestion storage.

ali_se: Draft checklist for CAIQ mapping:
- Encryption at rest (KMS): Responsibility -> Redwood infra for provider-managed; Customer for CMEK (when enabled).
- Logging & monitoring: Redwood maintains access/audit logs; full prompt retention is configurable (customer controls redaction).
- Data classification & retention: Customer must mark PII; we provide retention toggles and purge APIs.
- Change management/patching: Redwood owned.

sara_sales: Need exact CAIQ phrasing: buyer asked for table with column 'Control / Redwood responsibility / Customer responsibility / Evidence'. Can we produce that?

mike_security: Suggested wording snippet to reuse: "Redwood is responsible for runtime compute, infrastructure hardening, and secure storage of service-managed artifacts. Customers are responsible for the content they send to the service, their identity and access management, and configuration choices (e.g., retention, redaction). Customers may enable CMEK on Dedicated/Private; Hosted BYOK requires contract + ops setup." Use that across relevant controls. :thumbsup:

jamie_csm: They also want evidence for the POC — diagram + one-pager on KMS, plus a short screenshot of console options for retention toggles. Ali: can you include URLs or artifacts?

ali_se: I will produce: 1) PNG network/dataflow diagram, 2) CSV/CSV-format CAIQ mapping table, 3) 1-page KMS & logging FAQ. Need contact at buyer to validate network arrows.

sara_sales: Contact is dana@fintechco.com — I'll intro in the thread. Also note: pricing question — POC Dedicated needs a small commit. Will that impact CMEK availability?

mike_security: The capability is feature-gated. Ops needs to enable CMEK for the customer's Dedicated instance — not blocked by pricing technically but requires ticketing. I'll open/coordinate with ops.

ops-bot: deploy note: CMEK feature flag currently gated for non-prod. Please file ticket OPS-4821 to request enablement for customer Dedicated.

ali_se: Filing OPS-4821 now and starting the CAIQ table draft. Will post first pass here in the morning.

sara_sales: Perfect — appreciate it. I'll intro to Dana and ask for network diagram expectations.

mike_security: Also, for CAIQ Qs about model ownership: we should explicitly state we do not train on customer prompts and we don't persist prompt corpus for model training. Add that line to answers.

ali_se: Noted. I'll include a short 'we do not use customer prompts to retrain models' clause and point them to the Private/Dedicated options if they want stricter separation.

jamie_csm: Thanks — will review once Ali posts the draft. :raised_hands:
